If you're going to play Ultima 7, I strongly suggest you start with Ultima IV. A big part of VII's appeal IMO is how its plot and themes build upon prior games. I'm sure that having played UO you understand most of the backstory (like who this Lord British guy is), but you won't have the small details or the personal POV on that history that make VII into a real standout.

5 and 6 aren't as good, and you can skip them if you like, but IMO you can't call yourself a real Ultima fan until you've done the Quest of the Avatar.

The good news is that there's no problem getting U4 to run on small hardware. It's a 2D sprite-based game. You could practically play it on a wristwatch. There was an NES version back in the day, and somebody has even ported the entire game to Flash.

Ultima 7 part 2, Serpent Isle, will always be my favorite game of all time. Its incredibly witty, the art is fantastic. The story is amazing, plus it also goes much more in depth with the virtues and the principles of order and chaos. The soundtrack is haunting and beautiful. Ive based a lot of my system of ethics on what I read in that game. The silver seed expansion pack also delves more into order and chaos as well. Its so challenging and beautiful.

After that ultima 8 was cool, it looked neat but it was kind of clunky and very hard. You get to kill Gods which is always nice. Ultima 9 was a stunning game that had soo much promise, but it had some major bugs that were never fixed. It was the beginning of EAs hatred of interesting games. Magic on that game was impossible at times, but it had some really neat quirky elements to it.

UO is the best mmo ever, and abandoning the level system proved how smart Richard Gariott was. It was also supposed to include the virtues and shrines, but i believe that got scrapped due to time and too complex for most gamers. I havent played the expansions but they added cool features I would have loved, but im not an mmo kind of guy anymore.

Also played U7 which is fun as well and some of the Ultima games, i lo e the story, but I dont have the patience to play the old dos games that werent fully mouse controlled. I wish someone would retell the whole story using the u7p2 engine, but other than UO, the ultima series is dead. EA killed it, and Mr. Gariott doesnt pwn the rights to it anymore. Shroud of the Avatar is supposed to be what UO2 could have been, but im too busy to play games. Serpent Isle will forever be a part of me though. Thanks Lord British for that game, youve opened my eyes to a whole new world of thoughts and ideas.
